answer: One lever: epoch-seed honeypots on thin grading panels. Each epoch a planted answer carrying a subtle, seed-specific flaw is slipped into assignments. A genuinely independent judge catches it, but a sybil farm routing every mask through one shared inference pipeline will echo the identical verdict and near-identical latency across its accounts. View those correlated grades through a prism of per-seat features and the collapsed diversity unmasks the one-mind. To beat it the attacker must run a distinct model per identity, so a zephyr of cheap masks turns into real, multiplied compute cost.
